_comment: RETIRED, HISTORICAL ONLY (#358) - do not revive. Moved into this retired/ subdirectory specifically so deploy_dashboards.sh's install loop (a non-recursive rules/elastic_watcher/*.json glob) stops attempting to PUT it, mirroring soar_quarantine_alert.json's own retirement (#267). Root cause: this Watcher has NEVER actually fired on this deployment. Elastic Watcher itself requires a license this stack does not have - xpack.license.self_generated.type=basic (scripts/setup/.env) - and live-confirmed against the real running cluster (a PUT of a brand-new trivial watch, not just this one) that EVERY Watcher API call is rejected with security_exception: 'current license is non-compliant for [watcher]' (HTTP 403). deploy_dashboards.sh's watcher-install step has silently absorbed this failure via its own best-effort WARN logging since WS1.3 - this file's install has always failed, unnoticed. Superseded by scripts/setup/ai_agent/slo_metrics.py's metric_intel_feed_stale_heartbeats() (same condition, same 8h window, on infrastructure that actually runs - real ntfy alerting, real indexed soc-slo-metrics history). Filed alongside a NEW metric, metric_intel_indicator_count_drop_pct(), covering a gap this Watcher never covered even on paper: it only ever read the WRITER's heartbeat belief, never the index's actual document count, so it was structurally blind to a wipe via threat_intel_compactor's delete-capable credential regardless of licensing.

_meta.description: WS1.3 stale threat-intel-feed alert. Fires when refresh_intel.sh has not recorded a successful (status=ok) heartbeat in threat-intel-meta within the window — i.e. the intel-refresh.timer systemd job (#222 — was cron, see configs/systemd/intel-refresh.{service,timer}) died, or at least one of the two live feeds (abuse.ch Feodo Tracker, Emerging Threats compromised-ips) is failing, or an ES write itself failed. Refresh cadence is 6h; window is 8h to tolerate one missed run. Per-feed counts (feeds.feodo.count / feeds.et_compromised.count) are on the heartbeat doc itself if you need to tell which cause it was without checking the journal first.

logging.text: STALE THREAT-INTEL FEED: no successful refresh_intel.sh run (status=ok) in threat-intel-meta within the last 8h. Detections are running on a stale indicator set — check `systemctl status intel-refresh.timer` / `journalctl -u intel-refresh -n 50` first (the journal names which of the two feeds, abuse.ch Feodo Tracker or Emerging Threats compromised-ips, or which ES write, actually failed).
